srcdet: 9 real-world datasets: 8 from the KEEL-dataset repository, plus acl, which the authors of ref. [45] (Slowinski et al.) supplied. 30 synthetic 2-D datasets (sub-cluster, clover, paw shapes; IR 5 or 7; 5 disturbance ratios) come from the family in ref. [40]/[46] and are on the paper's web page. 36 noisy versions were built by adding class or attribute noise (20%, 40%) to the 9 real-world datasets.
crit: Real-world datasets: 'The choice of the real-world datasets was based on the work on imbalanced classification with noisy and borderline examples presented in [40]'; also 'As the number of noisy examples is quite high compared to the size of the minority class these data sets are chosen to study their impact.' Synthetic: 'This paper uses the family of synthetic datasets used in prior research on the role of borderline examples [40].'
benchmark_inherited_from: [40] K. Napierala, J. Stefanowski, S. Wilk, Learning from imbalanced data in presence of noisy and borderline examples (both the real-world selection and the synthetic family); synthetic generation details in [46] (Stefanowski)
imbalance_creation: Multi-class real-world datasets became binary by taking the union of one or more classes as positive and the rest as negative. Table 1 names each minority class (e.g. ecoli imU, newthyroid hyper, cleveland positive). Synthetic data were generated with 600 examples at IR=5 or 800 examples at IR=7, a minority class split into sub-regions (5 parts, or 3 for paw) inside a uniform majority, and borderline disturbance ratios DR = 0/30/50/60/70%. Noisy versions: class noise uses a pairwise scheme where a majority example is relabelled minority with probability x/100. Attribute noise: each attribute is corrupted separately in about x% of examples with a uniform random value (numeric) or a random domain value (nominal), x = 20% or 40%.
nominal_features: Kept, not encoded: SMOTE finds neighbours over numerical and nominal attributes with the HVDM metric. Attribute noise on nominal attributes picks a random value from the domain.
duplicates_or_filtering: Before experiments: not stated in paper. (The IPF / ENN / TL filters are part of the compared methods, not dataset cleaning.)
split_protocol: 5 runs of stratified 5-fold cross-validation, results averaged
ir_definition: IR = N- / N+, 'the relation between the majority class and minority class examples', where N- and N+ are the numbers of majority and minority examples; imbalanced when IR > 1

evidence.quote: This work focuses on binary classification problems (the minority versus the majority class) with examples randomly and uniformly distributed in the two-dimensional real-value space.
In such a way, 30 synthetic datasets with the above mentioned properties have been managed, all of which are available on the web-page associated with this paper.

In such a way, two different noise levels will be introduced into them: x = 20% and x = 40%. The introduction of noise consists of separately corrupting either the class labels or the attribute values

The choice of the real-world datasets was based on the work on imbalanced classification with noisy and borderline examples presented in [40].
As the number of noisy examples is quite high compared to the size of the minority class these data sets are chosen to study their impact.
This paper uses the family of synthetic datasets used in prior research on the role of borderline examples [40].
Multi-class datasets are modified to obtain two-class imbalanced problems, defining the joint of one or more classes as positive and the remainder as negative.

5 levels of DR are considered: 0%, 30%, 50%, 60% and 70%.
Class noise is introduced into the datasets following a pairwise scheme in which a majority class example has a probability of x/100 to be incorrectly labeled as belonging to the minority class.

Different re-sampling techniques to adjust the class distribution in the training data based on generalizations of SMOTE are studied in this paper.

notes: 75 is not printed as a total. It is the sum 30 synthetic + 9 real-world + 36 noisy (9 datasets x {class, attribute} noise x {20%, 40%}); the noisy sets are not named individually but appear in Table 9 as e.g. 'acl x=20%' under Class Noise / Attribute Noise headings. Text extraction mangled the synthetic names (e.g. 'sub  cluster IR=5, DR=0'); here they are normalised to 'sub-cluster IR=5, DR=0'. Table 1 prints 'breast' but the text calls it 'breast cancer'. The text says multi-class datasets were binarised but does not say which ones. Resampling-inside-folds is answered from the wording 'training data'; the paper never explicitly says the resampling is done inside each CV training fold. Printed page = PDF index + 183. The IPF parameters are set experimentally (Section 6.3). C4.5 is the main classifier; results for other classifiers are only on the web page.
